# System calls

A system call is a function built into Cogniscript. Call one by name, as you would a function of your own:
`string shout = StringToUpper(name);`. Pass every argument it takes, even one you leave empty: a script that
leaves one out fails to deploy, with "Argument count mismatch".

Which calls a script can make depends on where it runs:

| Library | Apps | Code-pipeline hooks |
|---|---|---|
| [Standard library](#standard-library) | yes | yes |
| [Maitento](#maitento) | yes |  |
| [Code pipeline hooks](#code-pipeline-hooks) |  | yes |

The language itself, with its types, statements and operators, is in [Cogniscript language](../index.md).

## Standard library

For apps and code-pipeline hooks.

### Strings

Search, compare, cut up, join and reshape text. See [Strings](strings.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`StringConcatenate`](strings.md#stringconcatenate) | Joins two pieces of text into one. |
| [`StringContains`](strings.md#stringcontains) | Whether text contains another piece of text. |
| [`StringEndsWith`](strings.md#stringendswith) | Whether text ends with a suffix. |
| [`StringIndexOf`](strings.md#stringindexof) | Returns the position of the first occurrence of one piece of text in another, counting from 0, or `-1` when it does not occur. |
| [`StringIsEmpty`](strings.md#stringisempty) | Whether text is empty or contains only white space, such as spaces, tabs and line breaks. |
| [`StringJoin`](strings.md#stringjoin) | Joins the items of a JSON array into one piece of text, with a separator between them. |
| [`StringLastIndexOf`](strings.md#stringlastindexof) | Returns the position of the last occurrence of one piece of text in another, counting from 0, or `-1` when it does not occur. |
| [`StringLength`](strings.md#stringlength) | Returns the number of characters in text. |
| [`StringPadLeft`](strings.md#stringpadleft) | Pads text on the left to a total length, for example to right-align numbers or add leading zeros. |
| [`StringPadRight`](strings.md#stringpadright) | Pads text on the right to a total length, for example to line up columns. |
| [`StringReplace`](strings.md#stringreplace) | Replaces every occurrence of one piece of text with another. |
| [`StringSplit`](strings.md#stringsplit) | Splits text at every occurrence of a separator and returns the parts as a JSON array of strings. |
| [`StringStartsWith`](strings.md#stringstartswith) | Whether text starts with a prefix. |
| [`StringSubstring`](strings.md#stringsubstring) | Returns part of text: the characters from a start position, counting from 0, either to the end or for a given length. |
| [`StringToLower`](strings.md#stringtolower) | Converts text to lower case. |
| [`StringToUpper`](strings.md#stringtoupper) | Converts text to upper case. |
| [`StringTrim`](strings.md#stringtrim) | Removes white space, such as spaces, tabs and line breaks, from both ends of text. |
| [`StringUnescape`](strings.md#stringunescape) | Turns backslash escapes in text, such as `\n`, `\t` and `\"`, into the characters they stand for. |

### JSON

Build JSON objects and arrays, read values out of them, and query or transform them. See [JSON](json.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`JsonArrayAdd`](json.md#jsonarrayadd) | Adds a value to the end of a JSON array and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonArrayCount`](json.md#jsonarraycount) | Returns the number of items in a JSON array. |
| [`JsonArrayCreate`](json.md#jsonarraycreate) | Returns a new, empty JSON array: `[]`. |
| [`JsonArrayGetAtIndex`](json.md#jsonarraygetatindex) | Returns the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0. |
| [`JsonArrayInsert`](json.md#jsonarrayinsert) | Inserts a JSON value into an array, before the item at a position, and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonArrayRemoveAtIndex`](json.md#jsonarrayremoveatindex) | Removes the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonArraySetAtIndex`](json.md#jsonarraysetatindex) | Replaces the item at a position in a JSON array, counting from 0, and returns the new array. |
| [`JsonAtaTransform`](json.md#jsonatatransform) | Evaluates a JSONata expression against JSON and returns the result as JSON text. |
| [`JsonIsParseable`](json.md#jsonisparseable) | Whether text is valid JSON of any kind: an object, an array, a string in quotes, a number, `true`, `false` or `null`. |
| [`JsonObjectCreate`](json.md#jsonobjectcreate) | Returns a new, empty JSON object: `{}`. |
| [`JsonObjectGet`](json.md#jsonobjectget) | Returns the value of a key in a JSON object, or empty text when the object has no such key. |
| [`JsonObjectSetBool`](json.md#jsonobjectsetbool) | Sets a key in a JSON object to `true` or `false`, and returns the new object. |
| [`JsonObjectSetString`](json.md#jsonobjectsetstring) | Sets a key in a JSON object to a string, and returns the new object. |
| [`JsonPathQuery`](json.md#jsonpathquery) | Runs a JSONPath query against a JSON object and returns what it selects, as JSON text. |
| [`JsonUnescapeString`](json.md#jsonunescapestring) | Reads a JSON string, quotes and all, and returns the text inside it with its escapes resolved. |

### Math

Round, compare and combine numbers, and pick random ones. See [Math](math.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`MathAbs`](math.md#mathabs) | Returns the absolute value of a number: `-2.5` gives `2.5`, and a positive number stays as it is. |
| [`MathCeiling`](math.md#mathceiling) | Rounds a number up to the next whole number: `2.1` gives `3`, and `-2.1` gives `-2`. |
| [`MathFloor`](math.md#mathfloor) | Rounds a number down to the whole number below it: `2.9` gives `2`, and `-2.1` gives `-3`. |
| [`MathMax`](math.md#mathmax) | Returns the larger of two numbers. |
| [`MathMin`](math.md#mathmin) | Returns the smaller of two numbers. |
| [`MathPow`](math.md#mathpow) | Raises a number to a power: `MathPow(2, 10)` is `1024`. |
| [`MathRandom`](math.md#mathrandom) | Returns a random whole number between two limits, both included, or a random fraction from 0 up to 1 when you give neither limit. |
| [`MathRound`](math.md#mathround) | Rounds a number to a number of decimal places. |
| [`MathSqrt`](math.md#mathsqrt) | Returns the square root of a number. |
| [`MathTruncate`](math.md#mathtruncate) | Drops the fractional part of a number, moving towards zero: `2.7` gives `2`, and `-2.7` gives `-2`. |

### Dates

Get the current time, move a date by days or hours, and take a date apart. See [Dates](dates.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`DateAddDays`](dates.md#dateadddays) | Adds a number of days to a date and returns the new date. |
| [`DateAddHours`](dates.md#dateaddhours) | Adds a number of hours to a date and returns the new date, moving to another day when it needs to. |
| [`DateDiff`](dates.md#datediff) | Returns the time between two dates in milliseconds: `left` minus `right`. |
| [`DateGetDay`](dates.md#dategetday) | Returns the day of the month of a date, from 1 to 31. |
| [`DateGetMonth`](dates.md#dategetmonth) | Returns the month of a date, from 1 (January) to 12 (December). |
| [`DateGetUtc`](dates.md#dategetutc) | Returns the current date and time in UTC. |
| [`DateGetYear`](dates.md#dategetyear) | Returns the year of a date, such as 2026. |

### Conversion

Turn values into text, and text back into numbers, dates, booleans and JSON. See [Conversion](conversion.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`BoolToString`](conversion.md#booltostring) | Converts a bool to the text `true` or `false`, always in lower case. |
| [`DateTimeToString`](conversion.md#datetimetostring) | Formats a date as text, in ISO 8601 form unless you give a format. |
| [`DecimalToString`](conversion.md#decimaltostring) | Formats a decimal number as text, with `.` as the decimal point. |
| [`IntToString`](conversion.md#inttostring) | Converts a whole number to text, such as `42` or `-7`. |
| [`JsonArrayToString`](conversion.md#jsonarraytostring) | Writes a JSON array as text, either compact on one line or indented over several. |
| [`JsonObjectToString`](conversion.md#jsonobjecttostring) | Writes a JSON object as text, either compact on one line or indented over several. |
| [`NumberToString`](conversion.md#numbertostring) | Formats a number as text, writing a whole number without decimal places. |
| [`StringToBool`](conversion.md#stringtobool) | Reads a bool from text. |
| [`StringToDateTime`](conversion.md#stringtodatetime) | Reads a date from text, in any common form or in the exact format you give. |
| [`StringToDecimal`](conversion.md#stringtodecimal) | Reads a decimal number from text, such as `3.14`, `-0.5` or `1e3`. |
| [`StringToInt`](conversion.md#stringtoint) | Reads a whole number from text, such as `42` or `-7`. |
| [`StringToJsonArray`](conversion.md#stringtojsonarray) | Checks that text is a JSON array and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonArray`. |
| [`StringToJsonObject`](conversion.md#stringtojsonobject) | Checks that text is a JSON object and returns it, ready to store in a `jsonObject`. |

### Type checks

Check what a value holds: a number, JSON, or nothing at all. See [Type checks](type-checks.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`TypeIsDecimal`](type-checks.md#typeisdecimal) | Whether text is a number that can be used where a `decimal` is expected, such as `3.14`, `-2` or `1,000`. |
| [`TypeIsInteger`](type-checks.md#typeisinteger) | Whether text is a whole number written plainly, such as `42` or `-7`. |
| [`TypeIsJson`](type-checks.md#typeisjson) | Whether text is valid JSON other than `null`: an object, an array, a string in quotes, a number, `true` or `false`. |
| [`TypeIsJsonArray`](type-checks.md#typeisjsonarray) | Whether text is a JSON array, such as `[1, 2]` or `[]`. |
| [`TypeIsJsonObject`](type-checks.md#typeisjsonobject) | Whether text is a JSON object, such as `{"name": "Ada"}` or `{}`. |
| [`TypeIsNull`](type-checks.md#typeisnull) | Whether a value is null. |

### Console output

Write to the run's console output, which the finished run reports. See [Console output](console.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`Print`](console.md#print) | Writes text to the run's console, without a line break. |
| [`PrintLine`](console.md#printline) | Writes text to the run's console, followed by a line break. |

### Tracing

Write diagnostic output, which the run reports apart from ordinary console output. See [Tracing](tracing.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`Trace`](tracing.md#trace) | Writes diagnostic text to the run's console, without a line break. |
| [`TraceLine`](tracing.md#traceline) | Writes diagnostic text to the run's console, followed by a line break. |

Read the last error, and pause a script. See [Miscellaneous](miscellaneous.md).

| Call | What it does |

## Maitento

For apps.

### Interactions

Start interactions, wait for their answers, and take part in a run that is going. See [Interactions](interactions.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`InteractionAddMessage`](interactions.md#interactionaddmessage) | Posts a message from a person into an interaction run that is still going. |
| [`InteractionAwait`](interactions.md#interactionawait) | Waits until an interaction run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run. |
| [`InteractionAwaitAll`](interactions.md#interactionawaitall) | Waits until every interaction run in a list has ended, then returns them all. |
| [`InteractionAwaitAny`](interactions.md#interactionawaitany) | Waits until at least one interaction run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then. |
| [`InteractionGet`](interactions.md#interactionget) | Returns an interaction's definition, with every version. |
| [`InteractionGetToolResult`](interactions.md#interactiongettoolresult) | Returns the stored result of one tool call in an interaction run. |
| [`InteractionList`](interactions.md#interactionlist) | Returns the interactions in a namespace. |
| [`InteractionProcessGet`](interactions.md#interactionprocessget) | Returns an interaction run as it is now, without waiting for it. |
| [`InteractionStart`](interactions.md#interactionstart) | Starts an interaction run and returns its id straight away, without waiting for its answer. |
| [`InteractionStartWithLoomGifts`](interactions.md#interactionstartwithloomgifts) | Starts an interaction run, as [`InteractionStart`](interactions.md#interactionstart) does, handing some of its agents threads of memory as they start; returns the run's id straight away. |
| [`InteractionStartWithSwarmLimits`](interactions.md#interactionstartwithswarmlimits) | Starts an interaction run, as [`InteractionStartWithLoomGifts`](interactions.md#interactionstartwithloomgifts) does, narrowing how far its sub-interactions may spread; returns the run's id straight away. |
| [`InteractionVoteNo`](interactions.md#interactionvoteno) | Votes no, as a person, on the vote or proposed solution an interaction run is waiting on, giving a reason. |
| [`InteractionVoteYes`](interactions.md#interactionvoteyes) | Votes yes, as a person, on the vote or proposed solution an interaction run is waiting on. |

### Apps

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`AppGet`](apps.md#appget) | Returns an app's definition, with every version. |
| [`AppList`](apps.md#applist) | Returns the apps in a namespace. |
| [`AppProcessAwait`](apps.md#appprocessawait) | Waits until an app run has ended (`Finished`, `Error` or `Killed`), then returns the run. |
| [`AppProcessAwaitAll`](apps.md#appprocessawaitall) | Waits until every app run in a list has ended, then returns them all. |
| [`AppProcessAwaitAny`](apps.md#appprocessawaitany) | Waits until at least one app run in a list has ended, then returns every run in the list that has ended by then. |
| [`AppProcessGet`](apps.md#appprocessget) | Returns an app run as it is now, without waiting for it. |
| [`AppStart`](apps.md#appstart) | Starts a run of an app and returns its id straight away, without waiting for it to finish. |
| [`AppStateGetInput`](apps.md#appstategetinput) | Returns the current value of one of this run's inputs. |
| [`AppStateSetInput`](apps.md#appstatesetinput) | Changes the stored value of one of this run's inputs. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputBool`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputbool) | Sets a named true-or-false output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputDate`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputdate) | Sets a named date output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputDecimal`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputdecimal) | Sets a named number output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputGuid`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputguid) | Sets a named id (`guid`) output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputInteger`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputinteger) | Sets a named whole-number output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputJsonArray`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputjsonarray) | Sets a named JSON array output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputJsonObject`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputjsonobject) | Sets a named JSON object output on this run. |
| [`AppStateSetOutputString`](apps.md#appstatesetoutputstring) | Sets a named text output on this run. |

### Automations

Create and change automations, their schedules and their triggers, and fire one. Automations are known as automated actions in Maitento, which is why the calls start with `Action`. See [Automations](automations.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ActionCreate`](automations.md#actioncreate) | Creates an automation, with the actions it starts when it is triggered, and returns it. |
| [`ActionDelete`](automations.md#actiondelete) | Deletes an automation, with its schedules, triggers and history. |
| [`ActionGet`](automations.md#actionget) | Returns an automation: its actions, schedules, triggers and recent history. |
| [`ActionHistory`](automations.md#actionhistory) | Returns the runs an automation has started, newest first. |
| [`ActionList`](automations.md#actionlist) | Returns the automations in a namespace, or in your whole tenant. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerAdd`](automations.md#actionmsgtriggeradd) | Adds a message trigger to an automation, so it starts whenever another run changes and matches a filter, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerDisable`](automations.md#actionmsgtriggerdisable) | Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerEnable`](automations.md#actionmsgtriggerenable) | Switches on one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionMsgTriggerRemove`](automations.md#actionmsgtriggerremove) | Removes one of an automation's message triggers, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleAdd`](automations.md#actionscheduleadd) | Adds a schedule to an automation, so it starts at the times a cron expression gives, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleDisable`](automations.md#actionscheduledisable) | Switches off, without removing it, one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleEnable`](automations.md#actionscheduleenable) | Switches on one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionScheduleRemove`](automations.md#actionscheduleremove) | Removes one of an automation's schedules, and returns the automation. |
| [`ActionTrigger`](automations.md#actiontrigger) | Triggers an automation by hand: starts each of its actions now, and returns the id of the first run it started, without waiting for it. |
| [`ActionUpdate`](automations.md#actionupdate) | Replaces an automation's name, description and actions, and returns it. |

### Sandboxes

Start sandboxes, run commands in them, and give them packages, users, files and secrets. Sandboxes are known as capsules in Maitento, which is why the calls start with `Capsule`. See [Sandboxes](sandboxes.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`CapsuleAddUser`](sandboxes.md#capsuleadduser) | Creates a Linux user in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleAwait`](sandboxes.md#capsuleawait) | Waits until a sandbox run has ended, then returns it as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleAwaitAll`](sandboxes.md#capsuleawaitall) | Waits until every one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns them all as a JSON array. |
| [`CapsuleAwaitAny`](sandboxes.md#capsuleawaitany) | Waits until at least one of several sandbox runs has ended, then returns the ones that have, as a JSON array. |
| [`CapsuleCommandAwait`](sandboxes.md#capsulecommandawait) | Waits until a command sent to a sandbox has ended, then returns it as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleCommandGet`](sandboxes.md#capsulecommandget) | Returns a command sent to a sandbox, with its status and output so far, as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleDefinitionGet`](sandboxes.md#capsuledefinitionget) | Returns a capsule, the recipe a sandbox starts from, as JSON. |
| [`CapsuleDefinitionList`](sandboxes.md#capsuledefinitionlist) | Lists capsules, the recipes sandboxes start from, as a JSON array. |
| [`CapsuleExec`](sandboxes.md#capsuleexec) | Sends a shell command to a sandbox and returns the command's id straight away, without waiting for it to run. |
| [`CapsuleGet`](sandboxes.md#capsuleget) | Returns a sandbox run as JSON: its status, what it has mounted, created and installed, and every command sent to it. |
| [`CapsuleInstallPackage`](sandboxes.md#capsuleinstallpackage) | Installs a Debian package with `apt` in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleMountSecret`](sandboxes.md#capsulemountsecret) | Writes a secret to a file in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleMountVfs`](sandboxes.md#capsulemountvfs) | Mounts a file system in a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleRemovePackage`](sandboxes.md#capsuleremovepackage) | Removes a Debian package from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleRemoveUser`](sandboxes.md#capsuleremoveuser) | Removes a Linux user from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleStart`](sandboxes.md#capsulestart) | Starts a sandbox from a capsule and returns the sandbox run's id straight away, without waiting for it to be ready. |
| [`CapsuleTerminate`](sandboxes.md#capsuleterminate) | Asks a running sandbox to stop, and returns the stop request's id straight away, without waiting for the sandbox to end. |
| [`CapsuleUnmountSecret`](sandboxes.md#capsuleunmountsecret) | Removes a secret's file from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleUnmountVfs`](sandboxes.md#capsuleunmountvfs) | Unmounts a file system from a running sandbox, and returns the operation's id straight away. |
| [`CapsuleWaitUntilStarted`](sandboxes.md#capsulewaituntilstarted) | Waits until a sandbox has started, then returns the sandbox run as JSON. |

### Memory

Create memory, and read and shape what it holds. Memory is known as looms in Maitento, which is why many of the calls start with `Loom`. See [Memory](memory.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`LoomCreate`](memory.md#loomcreate) | Creates a loom, a long-term memory for agents, and returns it as JSON. |
| [`LoomDelete`](memory.md#loomdelete) | Erases a loom and everything woven in it, for good. |
| [`LoomGet`](memory.md#loomget) | Finds a loom by its id or its name and returns it as JSON. |
| [`LoomList`](memory.md#loomlist) | Lists the looms in a namespace, sorted by name, as a JSON array. |
| [`LoomSeed`](memory.md#loomseed) | Copies the strongest shared knowledge of another loom into this one, and says how many threads it copied. |
| [`LoomSessions`](memory.md#loomsessions) | Lists the sessions agents have had with a loom, newest first, as a JSON array. |
| [`LoomUpdate`](memory.md#loomupdate) | Renames a loom, rewrites its description or changes its night-weaving settings, and returns the loom as JSON. |
| [`NightWeave`](memory.md#nightweave) | Asks for a loom to be night-woven now, without waiting for its quiet period. |
| [`NightWeavingList`](memory.md#nightweavinglist) | Lists a loom's night weavings, newest first, as a JSON array. |
| [`NightWeavingListSince`](memory.md#nightweavinglistsince) | Lists the night weavings of every loom in the tenant that changed at or after a given moment, oldest change first, as a JSON array. |
| [`PatternDelete`](memory.md#patterndelete) | Erases the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase. |
| [`PatternGet`](memory.md#patternget) | Returns the pattern a loom keeps for one codebase, as JSON. |
| [`PatternList`](memory.md#patternlist) | Lists the patterns a loom keeps, one per codebase, most recently changed first, as a JSON array. |
| [`PatternShape`](memory.md#patternshape) | Changes the pattern a loom keeps for a codebase, creating it if there is none, and returns the pattern as JSON. |
| [`ShuttleRetrieve`](memory.md#shuttleretrieve) | Searches a loom for the threads that matter to a question, best first, as a JSON array. |
| [`TapestryInspect`](memory.md#tapestryinspect) | Returns a loom's state as JSON: what it holds, what is held close, what is fading and what night weaving last did. |
| [`TapestryPanels`](memory.md#tapestrypanels) | Lists the portraits night weaving has written in a loom, one per person or thing, sorted by subject, as a JSON array. |
| [`TapestryReflect`](memory.md#tapestryreflect) | Gathers everything a loom holds about a topic, as JSON. |
| [`TapestryWeave`](memory.md#tapestryweave) | Writes the "What You Know" an agent would wake up with if the given people walked in now, and returns it as JSON. |
| [`TensionList`](memory.md#tensionlist) | Lists a loom's tensions, newest first, as a JSON array. |
| [`TensionResolve`](memory.md#tensionresolve) | Records how an open tension was resolved, and returns it with its two threads as JSON. |
| [`ThreadCut`](memory.md#threadcut) | Lets a thread go: its words are released, and a knot remains saying why. |
| [`ThreadGet`](memory.md#threadget) | Returns one thread of a loom as JSON. |
| [`ThreadGive`](memory.md#threadgive) | Gives a thread to another loom, where it arrives second-hand. |
| [`ThreadList`](memory.md#threadlist) | Lists a loom's threads, newest first unless sorted otherwise, as a JSON array. |
| [`ThreadPin`](memory.md#threadpin) | Pins a thread, so it is always part of what an agent wakes up knowing, or unpins it. |
| [`ThreadReframe`](memory.md#threadreframe) | Revises a thread: its wording, its weight, whether it is foundational, or the words it waits for. |
| [`ThreadUnravel`](memory.md#threadunravel) | Erases one thread for good, with any tension, portrait and pattern made from it. |
| [`ThreadWeave`](memory.md#threadweave) | Weaves a new thread into a loom, or strengthens the one it already has when it holds the same thing. |

### Namespaces

Create, read, list and update namespaces. See [Namespaces](namespaces.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`NamespaceCreate`](namespaces.md#namespacecreate) | Creates a namespace: a folder that apps, agents, file systems and the rest are deployed into. |
| [`NamespaceGet`](namespaces.md#namespaceget) | Gets a namespace by its name. |
| [`NamespaceList`](namespaces.md#namespacelist) | Lists every namespace in the tenant. |
| [`NamespaceUpdate`](namespaces.md#namespaceupdate) | Renames a namespace. |

### Knowledge bases

Create, list and delete knowledge bases. Knowledge bases are known as partitions in Maitento, which is why the calls start with `Partition`. See [Knowledge bases](knowledge-bases.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`PartitionCreate`](knowledge-bases.md#partitioncreate) | Creates an empty knowledge base, ready for files to be uploaded and indexed. |
| [`PartitionDelete`](knowledge-bases.md#partitiondelete) | Deletes an empty knowledge base. |
| [`PartitionList`](knowledge-bases.md#partitionlist) | Lists every knowledge base in the tenant, temporary ones included. |

### Runs

Stop a run. Runs are known as processes in Maitento. See [Runs](runs.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`ProcessKill`](runs.md#processkill) | Stops a run in your tenant: an app, interaction, sandbox (capsule) or code pipeline run. |

### Secrets

Create, list, update and delete secrets. See [Secrets](secrets.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`SecretCreate`](secrets.md#secretcreate) | Stores a new secret, such as an API key, for the tenant's tools and sandboxes to use by name. |
| [`SecretDelete`](secrets.md#secretdelete) | Deletes a secret. |
| [`SecretList`](secrets.md#secretlist) | Lists the tenant's secrets, without their values. |
| [`SecretUpdate`](secrets.md#secretupdate) | Renames a secret, gives it a new value, or both. |

### File systems

Create file systems, and read, write, find and move the files in them. The calls start with `Vfs`, for virtual file system. See [File systems](file-systems.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`VfsAppendLines`](file-systems.md#vfsappendlines) | Adds lines to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet. |
| [`VfsAppendText`](file-systems.md#vfsappendtext) | Adds text to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet. |
| [`VfsBatchEdit`](file-systems.md#vfsbatchedit) | Edits several text files in a file system in one call, each with its own list of operations. |
| [`VfsBatchRead`](file-systems.md#vfsbatchread) | Reads several text files from a file system in one call. |
| [`VfsCopy`](file-systems.md#vfscopy) | Copies a file or a directory to another path in the same file system. |
| [`VfsCreate`](file-systems.md#vfscreate) | Creates an empty file system in a namespace. |
| [`VfsDeleteDirectory`](file-systems.md#vfsdeletedirectory) | Deletes a directory from a file system. |
| [`VfsDeleteFile`](file-systems.md#vfsdeletefile) | Deletes a file from a file system. |
| [`VfsDestroy`](file-systems.md#vfsdestroy) | Deletes a file system and every file in it, permanently. |
| [`VfsEdit`](file-systems.md#vfsedit) | Edits a text file in a file system with a list of operations: find and replace, replace lines, insert lines or delete lines. |
| [`VfsExistsDirectory`](file-systems.md#vfsexistsdirectory) | Whether a directory exists at a path in a file system. |
| [`VfsExistsFile`](file-systems.md#vfsexistsfile) | Whether a file exists at a path in a file system. |
| [`VfsFind`](file-systems.md#vfsfind) | Searches a file system for files or directories by name, by content, or both. |
| [`VfsGet`](file-systems.md#vfsget) | Gets a file system's details by its name. |
| [`VfsListAll`](file-systems.md#vfslistall) | Lists the file systems in a namespace, or in the whole tenant. |
| [`VfsListDirectory`](file-systems.md#vfslistdirectory) | Lists what's directly in a directory of a file system: its files and directories, but not what's inside those. |
| [`VfsMkdir`](file-systems.md#vfsmkdir) | Creates a directory in a file system, with any parent directories it needs. |
| [`VfsMove`](file-systems.md#vfsmove) | Moves or renames a file or a directory within a file system. |
| [`VfsReadLines`](file-systems.md#vfsreadlines) | Reads a text file from a file system as a list of lines. |
| [`VfsReadText`](file-systems.md#vfsreadtext) | Reads a whole text file from a file system. |
| [`VfsTree`](file-systems.md#vfstree) | Lists a directory of a file system and everything below it, as a tree and as a flat list. |
| [`VfsWriteLines`](file-systems.md#vfswritelines) | Writes a list of lines to a file in a file system, replacing the file if it's there. |
| [`VfsWriteText`](file-systems.md#vfswritetext) | Writes text to a file in a file system, replacing the file if it's there. |

### Webhooks

Create, list, update and delete webhooks. See [Webhooks](webhooks.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`WebHookCreate`](webhooks.md#webhookcreate) | Registers a web hook: a URL that Maitento calls whenever something of one kind changes, such as an app run. |
| [`WebHookDelete`](webhooks.md#webhookdelete) | Deletes a web hook. |
| [`WebHookList`](webhooks.md#webhooklist) | Lists the tenant's web hooks. |
| [`WebHookUpdate`](webhooks.md#webhookupdate) | Changes a web hook's URL and secret. |

## Code pipeline hooks

For code-pipeline hooks.

Read a code pipeline run's inputs, variables and step results, set its variables, and write to its log, from a hook. See [Code pipeline hooks](code-pipeline-hooks.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`PipelineGetInput`](code-pipeline-hooks.md#pipelinegetinput) | Gets one of the inputs a code pipeline run was started with. |
| [`PipelineGetStepFailure`](code-pipeline-hooks.md#pipelinegetstepfailure) | Gets why one step of a code pipeline run failed. |
| [`PipelineGetStepOutput`](code-pipeline-hooks.md#pipelinegetstepoutput) | Gets the result of one step of a code pipeline run: its agent's final reply. |
| [`PipelineGetVariable`](code-pipeline-hooks.md#pipelinegetvariable) | Gets the value of one of a code pipeline run's variables. |
| [`PipelineLog`](code-pipeline-hooks.md#pipelinelog) | Writes a message to Maitento's own service log, tagged with the run's id. |
| [`PipelineSetVariable`](code-pipeline-hooks.md#pipelinesetvariable) | Sets one of a code pipeline run's variables, creating it if it isn't there. |

## Types in the signatures

Each call's signature uses the language's type keywords:

| Type | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `string` | Text. |
| `int` | A whole number, from -2147483648 to 2147483647. |
| `decimal` | A number with a fractional part, such as `2.5`, held exactly in base 10. |
| `bool` | `true` or `false`. |
| `guid` | An id, such as a run's or a file's, in the form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`. |
| `date` | A date and time. |
| `jsonObject` | A JSON object: named values inside `{ }`. |
| `jsonArray` | A JSON array: an ordered list of values inside `[ ]`. |
| `void` | No value: the return type of a function that returns nothing. |
